title: Make the website a citable source for buyer questions
finding: Client website cited as a source
evidence: 22% of 9 valid responses (sample-platform-a, sample-platform-b) (Limitation: Small samples; AI answers vary between runs, locations and accounts.)
business_relevance: Even when an AI answer mentions a brand, it may cite a directory or competitor instead of the brand’s own site.
action: Publish pages that directly answer the tested buyer questions (service + location + specifics). Review which domains are cited today and close the content gaps they reveal.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If the website directly answers the tested questions, the client domain may be cited more often. No outcome is guaranteed.

title: Add a genuine FAQ section to key service pages
evidence: No page with 3+ question headings or FAQPage markup
business_relevance: Buyers ask questions in natural language — the same way they ask AI assistants. Direct answers on your own pages give those systems something accurate to quote.
action: Collect the real questions your sales team hears and answer them on the relevant service pages. Mark up with FAQPage schema only if the Q&A is visible on the page.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If the site answers common buyer questions directly, it may be more likely to be cited for them. FAQ markup alone does not guarantee visibility.

title: Show business registration details and a privacy policy
evidence: GSTIN shown: no; privacy policy: no
business_relevance: GSTIN and a privacy policy are basic credibility signals for Indian B2B buyers and are expected under India’s data protection rules when collecting enquiries.
action: Display the GSTIN in the footer (if the business is comfortable doing so) and publish a privacy policy describing how enquiry data is used.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If identity signals are visible, cautious buyers may be more willing to submit an enquiry.

title: Name each core service in page titles and headings
evidence: full truckload: body text only; part load: body text only; container transport: not found; ODC transport: not found
business_relevance: Buyers search by service (“part load transport”, “customs clearance”). If the service is only mentioned in passing, the site is unlikely to match those searches or AI answers.
action: For every service marked ‘not found’ or ‘body text only’, add it to the title and H1 of the most relevant page.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If services are stated explicitly, the site may become eligible to appear for more service-specific queries.

title: Create a dedicated page for each core service
finding: Dedicated pages for each core service
evidence: 0 of 4 services have a dedicated page; missing: full truckload, part load, container transport, ODC transport
business_relevance: A single generic ‘Services’ page cannot answer specific buyer questions about each service.
action: Create one substantive page per missing service: what it covers, vehicle/equipment types, coverage, typical lead times, documents needed, and a quote CTA.
effort: Medium–High (1 page per day including review)
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If each service has a focused page, those pages may be cited or ranked for service-specific questions.

title: Cover the cities, states and routes you actually serve
finding: Target cities, states and routes covered
evidence: Mumbai: body text only; Pune: body text only; Nashik: not found; Gujarat: not found
business_relevance: Logistics buyers almost always search with a location or lane. Missing geography means missing the question entirely.
action: Add genuine coverage details (branches, lanes, transit times) for each target geography. Create route pages only where you operate regularly — avoid thin, copy-paste location pages.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If target locations and lanes are covered with real detail, the site may appear for more location-specific queries.

title: Strengthen the facts AI systems can find about the brand
evidence: 33% of 9 valid responses (sample-platform-a, sample-platform-b) (Limitation: Small samples; AI answers vary between runs, locations and accounts.)
business_relevance: When buyers ask AI assistants for logistics providers, brands that are not mentioned are not considered.
action: Make service, coverage and credibility facts explicit on the website; keep business listings consistent; earn mentions on relevant industry directories and associations. Re-test the same questions monthly.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If the brand’s facts are explicit and consistent across sources, mention rates may improve over subsequent test runs. No outcome is guaranteed.

title: Expand thin pages with useful, specific information
evidence: 3 of 5 pages have fewer than 250 words of visible text (Limitation: Word count is a proxy; it does not measure accuracy or usefulness.)
business_relevance: Short pages rarely answer a buyer’s real questions about capacity, coverage, timelines or documentation.
action: Expand each listed page to cover: who the service is for, what is included, coverage, typical transit/lead times, documentation, and FAQs. Use real operational detail.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If pages answer buyer questions directly, they are more likely to be used as a source for those questions.

title: Add Organization structured data that matches the page
evidence: No Organization or LocalBusiness JSON-LD detected
business_relevance: Structured data gives search engines an unambiguous record of the business name, URL, logo and contact points.
action: Add Organization (or LocalBusiness) JSON-LD with genuine name, URL, logo, phone and address. Never add ratings or reviews that are not shown on the page. Fix any JSON-LD that fails to parse.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If the entity is described consistently, search engines may associate the brand with its website more reliably. Structured data does not guarantee rich results or AI citations.

title: State clearly on the homepage what you do and where
finding: Homepage states what the company does
evidence: Homepage title/H1: “sample roadlines welcome to sample roadlines” — no service term found
business_relevance: Visitors and AI systems summarise a company from its homepage; a vague headline leads to vague or missing mentions.
action: Rewrite the homepage title and H1 to include the primary service and region, e.g. “Full Truckload & Part Load Transport across Maharashtra”.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If the homepage is explicit, summaries of the business may become more accurate.

title: Publish an XML sitemap
business_relevance: A sitemap helps search engines find every service, route and location page, not only those linked from the homepage.
action: Generate /sitemap.xml listing all canonical public pages, reference it in robots.txt and submit it in Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
effort: Low (1–2 hours; most CMSs have a plugin)
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If a sitemap is submitted, deeper pages such as route pages may be indexed more completely.

title: Write unique meta descriptions
evidence: 4 of 5 pages have a missing, poorly sized (outside 50–170 chars) or duplicated meta description
business_relevance: Meta descriptions shape the search snippet and help a buyer decide whether to enquire.
action: Write a 50–170 character description for each page summarising the service, coverage and the next step (call / quote).
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If snippets are specific, more qualified searchers may click through.

title: Make every page’s canonical URL point to itself
evidence: 4 of 5 pages lack a canonical tag, point it to another domain, or point it to a different URL; 4 inner page(s) declare the HOMEPAGE as canonical, which asks search engines to ignore them (Limitation: A canonical pointing elsewhere can be intentional for duplicate pages; confirm before changing.)
business_relevance: A missing or wrong canonical can split ranking signals across URL variants — or, if inner pages point to the homepage, tell search engines to ignore those pages entirely.
action: On each page, set <link rel="canonical"> to that page’s own preferred https URL. Only point elsewhere for genuine duplicates.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If duplicates consolidate, the preferred URL may accumulate signals more consistently.

title: Fix broken internal pages
finding: No broken internal pages among crawled URLs
evidence: 1 of 6 crawled internal URLs returned an error (4xx/5xx or fetch failure) (Limitation: Only crawled URLs were checked; internal URLs beyond the page limit were not tested.)
business_relevance: Broken pages waste crawl effort and lose buyers who click from navigation or search.
action: Restore or 301-redirect each failing URL to the most relevant live page, then update internal links.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If dead ends are removed, fewer visitors drop off before enquiring.

title: Add a WhatsApp contact option
business_relevance: Many Indian transport and freight buyers prefer WhatsApp for quick rate requests.
action: Add a wa.me link to a monitored business WhatsApp number with a pre-filled message, e.g. “Hi, I need a quote for…”.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If buyers can message in their preferred channel, enquiry volume from mobile may increase.

title: Structure pages with clear sections
finding: Clear heading structure (2+ H2s, no skipped levels)
evidence: 3 of 5 pages have at least two H2 sections without skipped heading levels
business_relevance: Clear H2 sections make pages easier for buyers to scan and for search systems to extract answers from.
action: Break pages into H2 sections (e.g. Coverage, Vehicle types, Process, Documents, FAQs) and do not skip heading levels.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If content is well structured, specific passages may be easier to surface for specific questions.

title: Write a unique, descriptive title for every page
evidence: 2 of 5 pages have a missing, too short/long (outside 10–65 chars) or duplicated title; 1 duplicated title text(s)
business_relevance: Titles are the first thing a buyer sees in search results; duplicated or vague titles make service pages indistinguishable.
action: Give each page a 10–65 character title naming the service and location, e.g. “FTL Truck Transport Mumbai to Pune | Company”.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If titles match how buyers search, click-through from search results may improve.

title: Use exactly one H1 per page
evidence: 1 of 5 pages have zero or multiple H1 headings
business_relevance: A single clear H1 tells search engines and AI systems what the page is about.
action: Make the main page heading the only H1 and convert other large headings to H2/H3.
expected_outcome_hypothesis: If page topics are unambiguous, the right page is more likely to be matched to the right query.
